delivered.text: Removing the `if (!job) return { status: 'missing' as const }` guard means `claim(id)` can return null, so `computeFee(job.amount)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'amount')` and callers branching on `status === 'missing'` are left with a dead branch as the return type collapses to `{ status: 'settled' }`. Restore the null guard before dereferencing `job`.

Changing the debit from `job.amount + fee` to `job.amount - fee` alters the amount posted to the ledger by `2 * fee`, under-debiting customers if the fee is meant to be added on top of the principal. Confirm the intended semantics of `computeFee`/`ledger.debit` and restore `job.amount + fee` if the fee should be added rather than subtracted.

The PR removed the `if (!job) { return { status: 'missing' as const }; }` guard, so `job` is now dereferenced unconditionally (`job.account`, `job.amount`) on the new `ledger.debit` line. Since `claim(id)` can return a falsy value, this throws a TypeError instead of returning `{ status: 'missing' }` and narrows the public return contract from `{ settled | missing }` to `{ settled }`; restore the guard before computing the fee and keep the `missing` variant in the return type.

The debit amount was changed from `job.amount + fee` to `job.amount - fee`, flipping the sign of the fee in the amount charged and under-charging by twice the fee if the original settlement was intended.
